chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman from Jarrah Al-Madaini from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
He said: 'One is not made to swear by other than Allah.' And he said: 'The Jew, the Christian, and the Magian are not to be made to swear except by Allah.'

key_terms.يُحْلَفُ: to be made to swear / to administer an oath

ai.seo_question: Who should be made to swear by Allah according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the universality of the divine name in oaths, extending the prohibition of swearing by other entities to include non-Muslims (People of the Book and Magians) to ensure their oaths are valid and binding. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that while specific religious figures may be invoked in certain contexts, the primary and most authentic oath remains by Allah alone, preserving theological consistency across different faiths. This ruling underscores the importance of sincerity and the avoidance of *shirk* in verbal commitments, a key theme in Islamic legal theory.
